widget_ast.title: Cumulative Progress S-Curve
widget_ast.data_qualification: Series are aligned on verified period end dates, not on week numbers: the baseline package uses baseline week numbering (week_num 1-62 from 2026-03-10) while the actual package uses reporting week numbering (week 17, week 18). The planned series uses supplied cumulative_planned_percent values for all baseline periods from 2026-03-10 up to the reporting cut-off date 2026-09-22 (baseline weeks 1-29); later baseline periods beyond the data date are excluded from this widget. The actual series is limited to the three cumulative actual periods supplied in actual_progress_package.actual_periods: the aggregated PRE_REPORTING period ending 2026-09-08 (cumulative 16.7812, covering 2026-03-10 to 2026-09-08), reporting week 17 ending 2026-09-15 (17.1619) and reporting week 18 ending 2026-09-22 (17.7389). No per-week actual cumulative history prior to 2026-09-08 was supplied, and no interpolation, back-filling or estimation of missing actual periods has been performed; those dates therefore carry a null actual value and the actual line consists of three supplied points. variance_pp is a direct display difference (actual minus planned) computed only at the three dates where both supplied values exist. Positive planned increments do not indicate ahead-of-schedule performance, and no performance status is asserted by this widget.

widget_ast.data_qualification: Periods were aligned by verified reporting period dates, not by week numbers: reporting week 17 (2026-09-09 to 2026-09-15) matches baseline week 28 and reporting week 18 (2026-09-16 to 2026-09-22) matches baseline week 29. Only these two reporting weeks have both a single-week planned value and a single-week actual value, so the chart is limited to two grouped periods. The actual package's PRE_REPORTING period (2026-03-10 to 2026-09-08, actual_percent_earned_in_period 16.7812) was excluded because it aggregates many baseline weeks and has no single-week planned counterpart; it was not decomposed or estimated. widget_ast.data_qualification: All ten phase identifiers (CN, EN, FTC, GN, HO, ML, MO, NOC, PL, PR) are present in both the baseline and actual progress packages, so every phase supplied by both packages is charted in source order. Planned and actual values are the supplied cumulative phase percentages at the 2026-09-22 data date and were not recalculated, reweighted or interpolated. The variance_pp values are direct display differences between comparable supplied planned and actual phase percentages and are labelled in percentage points; they are not a schedule-performance determination. Phase labels are activity-based phase codes from the source packages and do not represent engineering submission or approval statuses. Discipline-level and trade-level breakdowns are absent from both packages (empty disciplines and trades arrays), so this widget does not present discipline or trade comparisons. widget_ast.title: Phase Progress Variance
widget_ast.data_qualification: Phase rows are flat and are joined on the phase code supplied by both packages; all ten baseline phase codes (CN, EN, FTC, GN, HO, ML, MO, NOC, PL, PR) have a matching actual-phase record, so no comparison is missing. Phase display names were not supplied by the calculation packages, so only the supplied phase codes are shown. Variance is the authorized display difference of comparable supplied cumulative values (actual cumulative % minus planned cumulative %), expressed in percentage points; negative variance means actual cumulative progress is below planned cumulative progress for that phase. No weighted totals, phase aggregation, re-weighting or interpolation were performed. Phase ML carries zero total resource weight in both packages (13 unweighted activities), so its 0.0000 planned and 0.0000 actual values are reported as supplied but no variance is computed and the row is flagged partial; this does not indicate zero performance. Phases FTC and HO carry resource weight but both supplied percentages are 0.0000, so their zero variance reflects the supplied values. The actual phase percentages derive from 678 activities with progress rows against the 1,416-activity baseline; no adjustment or resourcing of missing progress rows was applied. All values are preserved at source precision; rounding for display is a renderer responsibility.
